To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
higher body mass index is associated with increased risk of hypertension among rural women in China.
higher BMI, even within ‘normal’ range (18.5 to 22.9 kg/m2) is associated with increased risk of hypertension among Chinese rural women.
a higher BMI, even within normal range, was associated with a significantly higher risk of hypertension in rural Chinese women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association between BMI and incident hypertension in Chinese rural women.
the relationship between obesity and hypertension.
the association between body-mass index and incident hypertension among rural women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
obesity is a major risk factor for hypertension, and that weight management is an effective strategy to reduce the risk of hypertension.
the relationship between BMI and hypertension risk is U-shaped.

(i) BMI is associated with the development of hypertension, even within the normal BMI category; (ii) the association between BMI and incident hypertension is consistent across all BMI categories; (iii) the association is not attenuated after adjustment for BP and other confounders; and (iv) this association is consistent among women of older age (⩾55 years).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
higher BMI was associated with increased risk of hypertension among rural women in the general population of China.
obesity is a major risk factor for hypertension, even among the normal BMI range.
the risk of hypertension is increased with higher BMI, even within normal BMI range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even within the normal range of body weight, a higher body weight is associated with an increased hypertension risk in rural women in Chinese population.
obesity is associated with a higher incidence of hypertension, even in women within the ‘normal weight’ range.
obesity is a risk factor for hypertension, even among those in the normal BMI range.
